mainTopic: The requirements and limits of liability for מולך, and why כרת is written three times for עבודה זרה
overview: The גמרא sets out exactly what makes a person liable for giving his child to מולך. He must hand the child to the כומרין, pass him through fire, and do it for מולך itself. A ברייתא learns each of these from the words of the פסוקים. Passing all of one's children is פטור. Grandchildren and children of flawed lineage do count, learned from the word 'offspring.' רב אשי's questions about a blind or sleeping child are never answered. אביי and רבא disagree about what the ritual looked like, and a ברייתא supports רבא: the child leaps over the fire, like children jumping over bonfires on פורים. The ברייתא also limits liability to one's own descendants. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees with it about passing oneself and about passing a child to other idols. Finally, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא explains why כרת is written three times for עבודה זרה, which leads to the dispute between רבי עקיבא and רבי ישמעאל over the doubled word הכרת תכרת.

steps.title: Liability requires handing the child to the idol's priests
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי rules that a person is only חייב for מולך once he hands his child over to the כומרין, learned from the word 'give' in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ינאי says: a person is not liable until he hands his child over to the כומרין (priests) of מולך, because the verse says, 'And of your offspring you shall not give to pass over to מולך.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי states a new rule: passing a child to מולך only makes a person חייב if he first hands the child over to the idol's priests.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from the word 'תתן' (give) in the פסוק. 'Giving' means handing the child over to someone, namely the כומרין. So the act of handing over is one of the required parts of the עבירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Priests of an idol (here, the priests of מולך)
The idol to which children were passed through fire
To pass over, to pass through

phrases.english: Rabbi Yannai says:
He is not liable until he hands him over to the priests,
phrases.notes: These are the priests of the מולך idol, and 'him' is the child.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "And of your offspring you shall not give
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:21

phrases.english: to pass over to Molekh."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיִּמְסְרֶנּוּ לְכוֹמָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion on the exact requirements for liability in מולך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for מולך requires handing the child over to the כומרין, learned from 'לא תתן.'

steps.title: A teaching supports the rule and lists the required parts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי ינאי. Each word of the פסוק adds a requirement: 'give' means handing over, 'to pass' means passing through, and 'to מולך' means it must be for מולך and not for another idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: One might think that if he passed the child but did not hand him over, he is liable. The verse says, 'You shall not give.' If he handed the child over to מולך but did not pass him, one might think he is liable. The verse says, 'To pass.' If he handed over and passed, but not to מולך, one might think he is liable. The verse says, 'To מולך.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רבי ינאי and shows that each word of the פסוק adds its own requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא follows a pattern: 'One might think he is חייב' in a case missing one piece, and then a word from the פסוק shows that this piece is needed. Passing without handing over is not enough ('give'), handing over without passing is not enough ('to pass'), and doing both for a different idol is not enough ('to מולך'). The first part proves רבי ינאי's point exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also taught this way (in a ברייתא), bringing support

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think each requirement alone makes him חייב. All of them are needed together: handing over, passing through, to מולך, and (in the next step) through fire.

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a baraita:
One might think: if he passed but did not hand over,
he should be liable?
The verse teaches: "You shall not give."
If he handed over to Molekh but did not pass,
one might think he should be liable?
The verse teaches: "To pass."
If he handed over and passed, not to Molekh,
one might think he should be liable?
The verse teaches: "To Molekh."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי ינאי's rule with a ברייתא and adds more requirements.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ינאי's rule that handing over to the כומרין is required.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that reads 'לא תתן' as excluding passing without handing over.

steps.title: Passing must be through fire, learned from a matching word
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: even after handing over and passing to מולך, he is only חייב if it was through fire. This is learned by a גזירה שוה from a פסוק in דברים, and the same comparison teaches that the פסוק in דברים also means מולך.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he handed over and passed the child to מולך, but not through fire, one might think he is liable. It says here 'to pass,' and it says there, 'There shall not be found among you one who passes his son or his daughter through the fire.' Just as there it is through fire, so too here it is through fire. And just as here it is to מולך, so too there it is to מולך.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds the last requirement: the child must be passed through fire. It proves this by comparing the word 'pass' in two פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our פסוק in ויקרא says 'to pass' but doesn't mention fire. The פסוק in דברים says 'passes...through the fire' but doesn't mention מולך. Because both use the same word, each one fills in what the other is missing: fire is needed here, and מולך is meant there.

keyTerms.meaning: It is said here (the start of a word comparison)
Learning from the same word appearing in two פסוקים

steps.whyThisMatters: The comparison works in both directions. It doesn't only add fire to our פסוק; it also limits the פסוק in דברים to מולך alone.

phrases.english: If he handed over and passed to Molekh, but not through fire –
one might think he should be liable?
It is stated here: "To pass,"
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our פסוק in ויקרא 18:21.

phrases.english: and it is stated there:
"There shall not be found among you one who passes
phrases.notes: דברים 18:10

phrases.english: his son or his daughter through the fire."
Just as there it is through fire,
so too here it is through fire.
And just as here it is Molekh,
so too there it is Molekh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, adding the fire requirement through a גזירה שוה.
steps.raayaObject: The requirement that the passing be through fire, and that דברים 18:10 refers to מולך.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A גזירה שוה on the word 'להעביר' between ויקרא 18:21 and דברים 18:10.
steps.whatToRemember: To be חייב for מולך, all four are needed: handing the child to the כומרין, passing him through, for מולך specifically, and through fire.

steps.title: Passing all one's children is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא rules that someone who passes ALL his offspring to מולך is פטור, because the פסוק says 'of your offspring,' meaning only some of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבא, says: If he passed all his offspring, he is exempt, because the verse says 'of your offspring,' and not 'all your offspring.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא adds a surprising rule: passing every one of your children to מולך does not carry the punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The prefix 'מ' in 'מזרעך' means 'from' or 'some of' your offspring. Since the תורה described the עבירה as giving part of one's children, giving all of them falls outside the exact wording of the punishment.
steps.confusionAlert: פטור here means he is exempt from the punishment for this specific עבירה. It does not mean the act is allowed.

phrases.english: Rav Aha, son of Rava, says:
If he passed all his offspring – he is exempt,
as it is stated: "Of your offspring" –
phrases.notes: The letter מ at the start means 'from,' meaning some of your children.

phrases.english: and not all your offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail from the same פסוק, this time an exemption based on the word 'מזרעך.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who passes all his offspring to מולך is פטור, since the פסוק says 'of your offspring' and not 'all your offspring.'

steps.title: רב אשי asks about a blind child, a sleeping child, and a grandchild
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether a person is חייב for מולך if the child he passed was blind or asleep, or if it was his grandchild.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: if he passed a blind child, what is the law? If the child was asleep, what is the law? If it was his son's son or his daughter's son, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks three open questions about unusual cases of מולך. The גמרא will now look for answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps showed that each word of the פסוק adds a requirement, like handing over and passing through fire. A blind or sleeping child cannot walk through on his own, so maybe it does not count as 'passing.' A grandchild raises a different question: is a grandchild included in 'his son or daughter'?

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question that is an open problem (a dilemma)
His son's son and his daughter's son, meaning his grandchildren

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
If he passed him while he was blind, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the child. The question is about a child who is blind.

phrases.english: If he was asleep, what is the law?
His son's son or his daughter's son, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier requirements of 'passing' and 'offspring' by asking about unclear edge cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is one חייב for מולך if the child was blind, was asleep, or was a grandchild?

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that grandchildren are included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers one of the three questions: a ברייתא learns from the word 'offspring' that passing a grandchild also makes one חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Resolve at least one question, as a ברייתא teaches: Why does the פסוק say 'Because he has given of his offspring to מולך'? Since the פסוק says 'There shall not be found among you one who passes his son or his daughter through fire,' I would only know about his son and daughter. From where do we know about his son's son and his daughter's son? The פסוק says 'When he gives of his offspring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the grandchild question using a ברייתא. Grandchildren count, because the פסוק says 'offspring,' and that word covers more than just sons and daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים only mentions 'his son or his daughter,' which would leave out grandchildren. The word 'offspring' (זרע) in ויקרא is broader and includes grandchildren. This settles only the third question; the blind and sleeping cases stay open.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
From where do we learn it?

steps.confusionAlert: Only the grandchild question is answered here. The questions about a blind child and a sleeping child are left unresolved.

phrases.english: Resolve at least one of them,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
"Because he has given of his offspring to מולך" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:3

phrases.english: why does the verse need to say this?
Because it is said,

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא יִמָּצֵא בְךָ מַעֲבִיר בְּנוֹ וּבִתּוֹ בָּאֵשׁ״,
phrases.english: "There shall not be found among you one who passes his son or his daughter through the fire,"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:10

phrases.english: I would only know about his son and his daughter.
From where do we know about his son's son and his daughter's son?
The verse says: "When he gives of his offspring."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:4

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the third of רב אשי's three questions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Passing a grandchild to מולך makes one חייב, learned from the word 'offspring'.

steps.title: Why does the ברייתא switch from one פסוק to another?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא opens with the phrase 'because of his offspring' but brings its proof from a different phrase, 'when he gives of his offspring.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא started with 'because of his offspring' and finished with 'when he gives of his offspring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices something odd in the ברייתא it just quoted. It asks why the ברייתא starts by asking about one פסוק and ends by proving from another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא asked what 'because he has given of his offspring' (ויקרא 20:3) comes to teach, but then brought its proof from a different פסוק, 'when he gives of his offspring' (ויקרא 20:4). The question and the proof seem to be about two different פסוקים. The גמרא wants to know why the ברייתא switches.

phrases.english: The תנא opened with "because of his offspring,"
and finished with "when he gives of his offspring."
phrases.notes: These are two different פסוקים, one right after the other in ויקרא 20.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא פָּתַח בְּ״כִּי מִזַּרְעוֹ״ וְסָלֵיק בְּ״תִתּוֹ מִזַּרְעוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the internal structure of the ברייתא brought in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The wording of the ברייתא in step 6
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא asks about one פסוק but brings its proof from a different פסוק, which seems inconsistent.

steps.title: The second פסוק teaches that children of flawed lineage are included
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the second פסוק belongs to a separate teaching: 'his offspring' alone would only cover children of proper lineage, and 'when he gives of his offspring' adds children of flawed lineage.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a different teaching: 'His offspring' would only include offspring of proper lineage. From where do we know offspring of flawed lineage? The פסוק says 'When he gives of his offspring.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא really has two teachings mixed together. The first פסוק teaches about grandchildren, and the second פסוק teaches about children of flawed lineage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grandchildren are learned from 'because of his offspring.' The second mention of 'offspring' adds offspring of flawed lineage, so one is חייב for passing them to מולך too. So each פסוק has its own job, and nothing is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: A different teaching learned from the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: One is חייב for passing to מולך not only a son or daughter, but also a grandchild (from 'because of his offspring') and a child of flawed lineage (from 'when he gives of his offspring'). The blind and sleeping cases stay unresolved.

phrases.english: It is for a different teaching:
"His offspring" – I would only know about offspring of proper lineage,
from where do we know about offspring of flawed lineage?
The verse says: "When he gives of his offspring."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by giving the second פסוק its own separate teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the second פסוק to a separate teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to use two פסוקים for one teaching, which would make one of them extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first פסוק includes grandchildren, and the second includes offspring of flawed lineage.

steps.title: Only the usual way of passing makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a person is חייב for מולך only if he passes the child in the normal ritual manner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: A person is not liable unless he passes the child in the usual way of passing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from רב יהודה about how the act must be done.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about which child counts. Now the focus is on the action itself. Only the standard ritual form of 'passing' makes a person חייב, not any passing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The usual, standard way of passing the child through the fire

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
He is not liable
unless he passes him in the usual way of passing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיַּעֲבִירֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from which child counts to how the act must be done
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for מולך requires passing the child in the standard ritual manner

steps.title: What does the usual way look like?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exactly 'the usual way of passing' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? (What does this usual way look like?)
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a clear picture of רב יהודה's rule. This sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said 'the usual way' but did not describe it. Without a description, nobody knows which acts count. Two אמוראים will each give a picture.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?

phrases.english: What is the case?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term used in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The physical form of דרך העברה

steps.title: אביי: walking a brick path between two fires
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the child walks along a row of bricks in the middle, with fire on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: A row of bricks in the middle, fire on this side and fire on that side.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his picture: the child is walked along a brick path between two fires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, 'passing' means walking through, between two lines of fire. The child does not go over the fire. He walks along a path in the middle.

keyTerms.meaning: A row or latticework of bricks

phrases.english: Abaye said:
a row of bricks in the middle,
fire on this side
and fire on that side.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The child is walked along a brick path between two fires

steps.title: רבא: jumping over the fire like on פורים
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the passing is like the jumps children made over bonfires on פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Like the leaping on פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different picture: the child jumps over the fire, the way children jumped over bonfires on פורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, 'passing' means leaping over a fire, not walking between fires. So the two אמוראים disagree about the actual action. This difference will matter in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the פורים jumping was forbidden. He is only using a familiar custom to show what the motion of the מולך ritual looked like.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Like the leaping of Purim.
phrases.notes: People used to light a fire in a pit on פורים, and children would jump over it for fun.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a competing answer to אביי's
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The child leaps over the fire, like the פורים jumping

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that passing the child by walking is פטור, which fits רבא's view that the act is a leap.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא like רבא: He is not liable unless he passes him in the usual way of passing. If he passed him on foot, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that agrees with רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says walking the child through is פטור. Walking is basically אביי's picture, so the ברייתא shows the real ritual is jumping, as רבא said.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him

steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the dispute between אביי and רבא in favor of רבא.

phrases.english: It was taught in accordance with Rava:
He is not liable
unless he passes him in the usual way of passing.
If he passed him on foot, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: Walking through is exactly what אביי described, so this line points to רבא's jumping.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רבא's answer over אביי's
steps.raayaObject: רבא's view that the passing is a leap
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא ruling that passing on foot is פטור

steps.title: Liable only for one's own children
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one is חייב only for passing his own children, not his parents or siblings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is liable only for those who come from his own body. How so? His son or daughter: liable. His father, mother, brother, or sister: exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא moves to a new point: which people a person is חייב for passing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of 'his offspring,' so only people who come from him count. Passing a son or daughter makes him חייב. Passing a parent or sibling does not, since they are not his offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who come out of his thigh: his own descendants

phrases.english: And he is not liable
except for those who come from his own body.
phrases.notes: Literally 'those who come out of his thigh,' meaning his children.

phrases.english: How so?
His son or his daughter: he is liable,
his father or his mother,
his brother or his sister: he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא עַל יוֹצְאֵי יְרֵיכוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same ברייתא continues with a new rule about who counts
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one's own descendants bring liability; parents and siblings do not

steps.title: Passing oneself: a dispute
steps.stepSummary: Someone who passes himself to מולך is פטור according to the ברייתא, but רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he passed himself, he is exempt. And רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון holds him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the case of a man who passes himself, and records a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's ruling of פטור fits the rule just stated: a person is not his own offspring. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees and holds that passing oneself also makes a person חייב.
steps.whatToRemember: For מולך: the act must be the usual leap over fire (like רבא), and liability is for one's own children, not parents or siblings. Passing oneself is disputed.

phrases.english: If he passed himself, he is exempt,
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon holds him liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶעֱבִיר עַצְמוֹ – פָּטוּר, וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מְחַיֵּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further case to the list of who counts, with a dissenting view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Passing oneself is פטור according to the ברייתא; רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון holds חייב

steps.title: Passing a child to other idols, not just מולך
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that passing a child to מולך or to any other idol makes one חייב. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says only passing to מולך makes one חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whether someone passes his child to מולך or to any other idol, he is liable. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון says: to מולך he is liable, but not to מולך he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going with one more rule: does this sin apply only to מולך, or also to other idols?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says the act of passing a child through fire is forbidden no matter which idol it is for. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון limits it to מולך alone, since that is the idol the פסוק names. So he is stricter about passing oneself (Step 15) but more lenient about other idols.

keyTerms.meaning: Other kinds of idol worship besides מולך

phrases.english: Both one who passes his child to Molekh,
and one who passes him to other idol worship, is liable.
Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, says:
To Molekh, he is liable;
not to Molekh, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד לַמּוֹלֶךְ, וְאֶחָד לִשְׁאָר עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא from Steps 13-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Passing a child to any idol makes one חייב. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון limits this to מולך.

steps.title: עולא asks for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's reason
steps.stepSummary: עולא asks what the source is for רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: What is the reason of רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: עולא opens a question. He is setting up his explanation of why רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון rules the way he does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון's ruling in Step 15, that one who passes himself to מולך is חייב. It is not about the ruling on other idols in Step 16.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though this comes right after the line about other idols, עולא is explaining the earlier ruling that passing oneself is חייב (Step 15).

phrases.english: Ulla says:

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the ruling that someone who passes himself to מולך is חייב.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the self-passing ruling in Step 15 to find its source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק behind the view that passing oneself to מולך is חייב.

steps.title: The word 'among you' means 'yourself'
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the פסוק says 'לא ימצא בך.' He reads 'בך' as 'in yourself,' which includes passing oneself.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says, 'There shall not be found among you.' 'Among you' means you yourself.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives the source: one word in the פסוק teaches that a person who passes himself is also included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים forbids passing 'your son or daughter.' רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reads the extra word 'בְּךָ' as adding the person himself.

keyTerms.meaning: There shall not be found among you

phrases.english: The verse states: "There shall not be found among you"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:10

phrases.english: "Among you" means: in yourself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers עולא's question in Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'בְּךָ' is read as 'yourself,' so passing oneself is included.

steps.title: Don't the רבנן also read 'among you' as 'yourself'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the רבנן reject this reading. In the case of lost objects, רב יהודה uses 'בך' in 'אפס כי לא יהיה בך אביון' to teach that one's own loss comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't the רבנן also learn from 'among you'? But we learned in a משנה: if one has his own lost item and his father's lost item, his own comes first. We asked why, and רב יהודה said: the פסוק says, 'Only so that there shall be no needy among you.' So his own comes before anyone else's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks: if the רבנן do not read 'בְּךָ' as 'yourself,' why does the halacha about lost objects seem to use exactly that reading?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say passing oneself is פטור, so they seem not to learn 'yourself' from 'בְּךָ.' Yet the accepted rule in בבא מציעא, that your own lost item comes first, seems built on 'בְּךָ' meaning 'you yourself.' That would show everyone uses this reading.

phrases.english: And do the Rabbis not interpret "among you"?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
His lost item and his father's lost item:
his own takes precedence.
And we said: What is the reason?
And Rav Yehuda said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר קְרָא ״אֶפֶס כִּי לֹא יִהְיֶה בְּךָ אֶבְיוֹן״ –
phrases.english: The verse states: "Only so that there shall be no needy among you"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:4

phrases.english: His own takes precedence over that of any person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption that only רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון reads 'בְּךָ' as 'yourself.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied position that the רבנן do not read 'בְּךָ' as 'yourself.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The rule that one's own lost item comes first is learned from 'בְּךָ' in a different פסוק. That shows the reading 'yourself' is accepted, so the רבנן should also say passing oneself is חייב.

steps.title: The lost-object rule comes from 'אפס'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that in the lost-object case, the lesson comes from the limiting word 'אפס,' not from 'בך.'
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the rule is learned from the word 'אפס' (only).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the רבנן: their rule about lost objects does not depend on the word 'בְּךָ' at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אֶפֶס' is a limiting word, and it teaches that one should first protect himself from becoming poor. So the רבנן can still refuse to read 'בְּךָ' as 'yourself' in the מולך פסוק. Their view that passing oneself is פטור stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון learns from 'בְּךָ' that passing oneself to מולך is חייב. The רבנן do not learn this. Their rule that one's own lost item comes first is based on the word 'אֶפֶס' instead.

phrases.english: There, it is from "only."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source: the lesson comes from another word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lost-object rule depends on reading 'בְּךָ' as 'yourself.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The lost-object rule comes from 'אֶפֶס,' so the רבנן need not read 'בְּךָ' as 'yourself.'

steps.title: Why does the תורה mention כרת three times for idol worship?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא asks why the תורה writes the punishment of כרת three separate times about עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: Why are there three mentions of כרת about idol worship?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא asks why the תורה repeats the punishment of כרת three times for עבודה זרה, and he is setting up his own answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea behind the question is that the תורה does not repeat itself for nothing. If כרת is written three times, each mention should teach something new. The next step tells us what each one teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Being cut off. A heavenly punishment for very serious sins.
More than one mention of כרת.
Why? Here it asks what each repetition is for.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
Why are there three mentions of karet regarding idol worship?
phrases.notes: Two are said about מולך (ויקרא 20:3, 20:5), and one about the מגדף (במדבר 15:30).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement after the discussion of the word 'בך' in steps 17-20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What each of the three mentions of כרת about עבודה זרה is meant to teach.

steps.title: Each כרת teaches a different case
steps.stepSummary: One כרת is for worship in the idol's normal way, one is for worship not in its normal way, and one is for מולך.
steps.simpleTranslation: One is for worship in its normal way, one is for worship not in its normal way, and one is for מולך.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא answers his own question. He gives each of the three mentions of כרת its own job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כדרכה' means serving an idol the way that idol is normally served. 'שלא כדרכה' means serving it in a way that is not its usual service. The third mention is for the act of מולך, passing a child to מולך.

keyTerms.meaning: In its normal way. Serving an idol the way it is usually worshipped.
Not in its normal way. Serving an idol with an act that is not its usual service.

steps.whatToRemember: Three mentions of כרת give three cases: worship in its normal way, worship not in its normal way, and מולך.

phrases.english: One is for worship in its typical manner,
and one is for worship not in its typical manner,
and one is for Molekh.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחַת לִכְדַרְכָּהּ, וְאַחַת לְשֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ, וְאַחַת לַמּוֹלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The three mentions of כרת teach: worship in its normal way, worship not in its normal way, and מולך.

steps.title: If מולך is idol worship, why does it need its own כרת?
steps.stepSummary: Some hold that מולך is a type of עבודה זרה. If so, the general כרת for idol worship should already cover it, so why does the תורה give מולך a separate כרת?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says מולך is idol worship, why do I need a כרת for מולך?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's list using the view that מולך is a kind of עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מולך counts as idol worship, the first two mentions of כרת (normal way and not normal way) already include it. That would make the third mention, the one for מולך, seem unneeded. So the גמרא asks what that third mention adds.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says. Used to test an idea against a particular opinion.
Why do I need it? Asks what a verse or rule adds that we did not already know.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מוֹלֶךְ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הִיא,
phrases.english: And according to the one who says Molekh is idol worship,
why do I need karet for Molekh?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר מוֹלֶךְ עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הִיא, כָּרֵת בְּמוֹלֶךְ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the third item in step 22's list according to one opinion about מולך.
steps.kashyaTarget: The separate כרת for מולך in רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's list.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מולך is a type of idol worship, the general mentions of כרת already cover it, so a separate mention seems extra.

steps.title: The מולך כרת is for passing a child to a different idol
steps.stepSummary: Even if מולך counts as idol worship, the extra כרת teaches about someone who passes his child to some other idol, where that is not its normal way of worship.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is for someone who passes his son in a way that is not that idol's normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The extra כרת is needed for a new case: passing a child to a different idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Passing a child through the fire is the normal service of מולך, but it is not the normal service of other idols. The extra כרת teaches that passing a child to any idol is still punished with כרת. This fits the view in the ברייתא (step 16) that passing a child to any idol makes one חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: One who passes his son through the fire. This is the act of מולך.

steps.confusionAlert: 'שלא כדרכה' here does not mean a strange way of doing מולך. It means passing the child to a different idol, where passing is not that idol's usual service.

phrases.english: For one who passes his son not in its typical manner.
phrases.notes: He means passing the child to a different idol, which is not usually served this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23 by giving the מולך כרת a new job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra verse a new application.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If מולך is idol worship, its separate כרת seems to add nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The separate כרת teaches that passing a child to any other idol also brings כרת.

steps.title: If the מגדף is an idol worshipper, why does he need his own כרת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about the מגדף: according to the view that the מגדף verse is about idol worship, why is כרת mentioned there?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says the מגדף is an idol worshipper, why do I need כרת for the מגדף?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a second, similar challenge, this time about the verse of the מגדף. The answer comes in the next part of the sugya.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One view holds that the מגדף verse is not about cursing ה׳ but about serving idols. If so, that כרת is about idol worship, which other verses already cover. The גמרא asks what this mention adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Usually, one who curses ה׳. Some read the verse as being about an idol worshipper.

phrases.aramaic: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר: מְגַדֵּף עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הִיא,
phrases.english: And according to the one who says the blasphemer refers to idol worship,
why do I need karet for the blasphemer?
phrases.notes: This is the כרת in במדבר 15:30.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר: מְגַדֵּף עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הִיא, כָּרֵת בִּמְגַדֵּף לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the same pattern as step 23, now applied to the מגדף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The mention of כרת in the verse of the מגדף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the מגדף is an idol worshipper, other verses already give כרת for idol worship, so this mention seems extra.

steps.title: The extra כרת teaches punishment in this world and the next
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the כרת in the מגדף verse is needed for a ברייתא. There רבי עקיבא learns from the double phrase הכרת תכרת that the sinner is cut off both in עולם הזה and in עולם הבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: "הכרת תכרת" (he shall surely be cut off). "הכרת" means in this world, and "תכרת" means in the World to Come. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 25. The כרת in the מגדף verse is not extra, because it is needed to teach a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was why the מגדף verse needs to say כרת at all. The answer is that its doubled wording, הכרת תכרת, gives us two separate lessons. According to רבי עקיבא, one word means the sinner is cut off in עולם הזה, and the other means he is cut off in עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for what is taught in a ברייתא
He shall surely be cut off. The verb appears twice.
This world, meaning his life here

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two words. In Hebrew, הכרת and תכרת are two forms of the same verb ('cut off'). רבי עקיבא gives each form its own separate meaning.

phrases.english: It is needed for that which is taught in a ברייתא:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is answering step 25. The כרת in the מגדף verse is needed to teach this ברייתא.

phrases.english: "He shall surely be cut off."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:31

phrases.english: "Hikkaret": he is cut off in this world;
"Tikkaret": he is cut off in the World to Come;
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25 by showing a separate lesson that the כרת wording teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The wording is needed for a different lesson, about where the punishment happens.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כרת in the מגדף verse looked extra and unnecessary.
steps.terutzMaskana: The doubled כרת teaches that the sinner is cut off both in עולם הזה and in עולם הבא.

steps.title: There cannot be three worlds of punishment
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל challenges רבי עקיבא. The previous verse already says ונכרתה, so if every word for כרת teaches a different world, there would be three worlds, which makes no sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said to him: But it already says "ונכרתה" (and that soul shall be cut off)! Are there three worlds?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל attacks רבי עקיבא's reading. There are really three words for כרת here, not two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every word for כרת gets its own meaning, ונכרתה in the earlier verse would need a world too. That gives three worlds, but there are only two, עולם הזה and עולם הבא. So רבי עקיבא's method of counting the words cannot work as it stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that...? (the opening of a challenge)
And that soul shall be cut off

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said to him:
But isn't it already stated: "and that soul shall be cut off"!
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:30, the verse right before הכרת תכרת.

phrases.english: Are there then three worlds?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: וַהֲלֹא כְּבָר נֶאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's reading in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading that הכרת and תכרת each teach a separate world
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counting ונכרתה as well, his method would need three worlds of punishment, and there are only two.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's reading: the Torah speaks like people speak
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל gives his own reading. ונכרתה teaches כרת in עולם הזה, and הכרת teaches כרת in עולם הבא. תכרת teaches nothing extra, because the תורה speaks the way people normally speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: "ונכרתה" means in this world, "הכרת" means in the World to Come, and for "תכרת", the תורה spoke in the language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל fixes the problem he raised. He gives only two of the three words a meaning and treats the last word as normal speech.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are still two lessons, עולם הזה and עולם הבא, but they come from ונכרתה and הכרת instead of הכרת and תכרת. The doubled verb תכרת is just the normal way people speak for emphasis, so nothing new is learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה spoke in the language of people. Not every repeated word teaches a new law.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: הכרת = עולם הזה, תכרת = עולם הבא. רבי ישמעאל: ונכרתה = עולם הזה, הכרת = עולם הבא, and תכרת is just normal speech (דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם). Either way, the כרת wording in the מגדף verse is needed, which answers step 25.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a classic source for רבי ישמעאל's famous rule, דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם. It is a basic disagreement about whether every doubled word in the תורה must teach something.

phrases.english: Rather, "and that soul shall be cut off": in this world;
"Hikkaret": in the World to Come;
"Tikkaret": the Torah spoke in the language of people.
phrases.notes: This extra word teaches nothing new. People often double a verb for emphasis, and the תורה does too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his challenge in step 27, רבי ישמעאל offers his own way to read the three words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ונכרתה = כרת in עולם הזה; הכרת = כרת in עולם הבא; תכרת teaches nothing new because דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם.
